documents.title: Clarification sought from Advance Agrolife Ltd
Compliances-Certificate under Reg. 74 (5) of SEBI (DP) Regulations, 2018

analysis.summary: Advance Agrolife Limited reported its highest ever quarterly performance for Q1 FY27, with revenue reaching Rs 3,304 million and PAT at Rs 225.5 million. Management highlighted ongoing backward integration, capacity expansions in technicals such as 2,4-D and Pretilachlor, and strategic new facilities including Unit-4 and Unit-5. The company aims to increase its export share to 20% by FY29 while leveraging structural cost advantages from its geographic presence in Jaipur. Furthermore, leadership remains optimistic about navigating global uncertainties and meeting rising market demand. Advance Agrolife reported its financial results for the quarter and year ended March 31, 2026, highlighting growth in revenue, EBITDA, and PAT.

demand_outlook.claim: Q3 FY26 income increased by 18 percent year-on-year due to higher demand and new customer additions.
demand_outlook.quote: • AAL’s Q3 FY26 Income at ₹ 1338 million increased by 18% Y-o-Y on the back of increased demand and addition of new customers.

capex_expansion.quote: AAL aims to commence operations at our new Unit-4 technical manufacturing facility at Gidhani by Q2 FY27, with an estimated first-phase capital expenditure of approximately ¥ 250 million.

capex_expansion.quote: AAL is in the process of setting up a 3.75 MW solar power plant with the objective of increasing the use of renewable energy and reducing its carbon footprint.

capex_expansion.claim: The company entered into an MOU to acquire land measuring 17,491.02 sq. mtrs. for Unit-5 at Dahej II GIDC Industrial Estate, Bharuch, Gujarat for manufacturing technical grade pesticides.

capex_expansion.quote: • The company is considering setting up of manufacturing facilities for Pretilachlor and PEDA, with installed production capacities of about 13 tonnes per day and 10 tonnes per day respectively.
